key_insight: A mixed finite element framework couples sediment concentration, temperature, velocity, and pressure to model heat-assisted consolidation–sedimentation.
engineering_relevance: The model supports simulation of thermally assisted settling of mineral suspensions, accounting for interactions between heat transport and sedimentation.
method: Formulate the quasi-stationary coupled system using pseudostress and concentration and temperature gradient variables.
Establish continuous well-posedness via Babuška–Brezzi theory and Banach’s fixed-point theorem under stated assumptions.
Analyze a mixed finite element discretization using Brouwer’s theorem and derive Céa-type and a priori error estimates.
evidence_signal: Numerical examples demonstrate model performance and confirm theoretical convergence rates; the abstract reports no experimental validation.
watch_item: Continuous existence and uniqueness require small-data and additional solution-regularity assumptions, limiting guarantees outside those conditions.
paper_title: Mixed finite element methods for a heat-assisted model of sedimentation
